newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares extend losses at close, Wall St weighs.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares extend losses at close, Wall St weighs.

text.p: Italian stocks extended losses but ended off session lows on Wednesday in a lethargic, technical market with Wall Street's fall weighing on sentiment, traders said.
"On a chart basis the outlook was already shaky and encouraged a fair amount of profit-taking, and Wall Street gave a push to further extend losses," one dealer said.
Bourse futures also lost ground with the FIB index falling below the 15,500 support level.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 1.25 percent down at 10,294 after a session low at 10,285, and the Mib30 blue chip index closed off 1.23 percent at 15,382 after a low at 15,362.
Traders noted the Italian debt market was softer at the close but Btp bond futures were steady around lower levels at 127.85 with a similar lack of concrete direction.
"The stock market saw a lot of arbitrage with bourse futures and there was very little to move the market," one said. Traded volume was estimated at around 600 billion lire.
Most blue chips saw selling. Energy group ENI slipped 0.28 percent to 7,903 lire and Fiat ended 0.78 percent down at 4,441.
Telecoms were all weaker, with Stet holding off 2.64 percent at 6,298 lire and mobile phone operator TIM down 1.38 percent at 3,496.
Saipem, the oilfield services arm of Italian energy group ENI, ended 5.2 percent down at 6,658 lire following press reports of flat 1996 profits, traders said.
The reports forecast Saipem's full-year profit in line with 1995's 168.6 billion lire, which was up 11 percent on 1994.

Financial holding group Gemina lost 2.34 percent to 776.1 lire after rising on Tuesday ahead of Thursday's shareholders' meeting to approve the hiving off of its industrial assets into a new company, HPI.
